transcript:
Clinician: Good morning, I'm Dr. Alvarez. Can you confirm your full name and date of birth for me?
Patient: Sure. Rosa Delgado, March third, nineteen sixty-one.
Clinician: Thank you, Rosa. What brings you in today?
Patient: The cough. It started about two weeks ago, mostly at night. My nose runs all day too.
Clinician: Anything you've been taking for it?
Patient: Allegra in the morning. It helps with the sneezing but not the cough.
Clinician: Any fever, chest pain, shortness of breath?
Patient: No fever. A little wheezy when I climb the stairs at work.
Clinician: Your lungs sound mostly clear, with a faint wheeze on the left. I think this is allergic, with some reactive airway. Let's keep the Allegra, add Flonase once a day, and an albuterol inhaler for the wheeze. If it isn't better by April 10th, come back and we'll get a chest X-ray.
Patient: Okay. Can the pharmacy call me? My cell is 937-555-0142.

Clinician: Hi Mr. Okafor, good to see you again. I'm going to read back what the front desk has: medical record number HL4471920, still at 2215 Wexford Avenue?
Patient: That's right. Same place since 2019.
Clinician: Your A1c came back at 7.9, up from 7.1 in the spring. How has the metformin been going?
Patient: Honestly I miss the evening dose a lot. My wife Adaeze reminds me, but she's been traveling.
Clinician: That's common. I'd like to add Jardiance, once a day in the morning, so the evening dose matters less. Any burning when you urinate, any infections?
Patient: No.
Clinician: Good. We'll recheck the A1c in three months. Dr. Brandt in cardiology also wants to see you about the blood pressure, his office will reach out.
Patient: Send it to my email, daniel.okafor58@gmail.com. I never pick up unknown numbers.

Clinician: Welcome to Northgate Family Practice. I'm Keisha, a nurse practitioner. Let's start with the basics. Name?
Patient: Margaret Lindqvist. Most people call me Peggy.
Clinician: And your date of birth?
Patient: The twelfth of June, nineteen fifty-two.
Clinician: Social security number for the insurance file?
Patient: four one two, six seven, three three nine eight.
Clinician: And your insurance member ID?
Patient: It's on the card. BCX 559 210 774.
Clinician: Thank you. Any medicines you take every day?
Patient: Lisinopril for blood pressure and Lyrica for the nerve pain in my feet.
Clinician: Who should we call in an emergency?
Patient: My son, Erik. His number is nine three seven, five five five, zero one eight eight.
Clinician: Got it. We'll get you set up with Dr. Mehta as your primary.

transcript:
Clinician: Hi, I'm Dr. Mehta. You're Tomasz Wilk?
Patient: Yes. I fell off a ladder on September 9th, cleaning the gutters.
Clinician: Which knee?
Patient: The right one. It swells up every evening. I've been taking ibuprofen, maybe four a day.
Clinician: Four a day is a lot for your stomach. Any locking or giving way?
Patient: It gave out on the stairs once.
Clinician: On exam there's an effusion and some tenderness on the inside of the joint. I want an MRI to look at the meniscus. Our scheduler will call you. Is (614) 555-0199 still good?
Patient: Yes. Or my daughter Hanna at 614-555-0123, she drives me.
Clinician: In the meantime, ice, keep it raised, and switch to Tylenol so you can drop the ibuprofen.

Clinician: Mrs. Haddad, this is a quick refill visit?
Patient: Yes, the levothyroxine and the atorvastatin. I'm down to three pills.
Clinician: Your thyroid level from August 28 was normal, so we'll keep the same dose. Cholesterol looks better too.
Patient: Good. Can you send it to the pharmacy on Shroyer Road?
Clinician: The one near Kettering? Sure.
Patient: That one. And my chart should say Leila Haddad, with two d's. Last time they spelled it wrong.
Clinician: I see it spelled correctly here. Your medical record number is HL3308114, I'll put that on the prescription.
Patient: Thank you. I'll be in Columbus visiting my sister until the end of the month.

Clinician: Tell me about the chest tightness.
Patient: It comes when I walk the dog fast. Goes away when I stop. Started around the first of October.
Clinician: Any history of heart trouble in the family?
Patient: My father had a bypass at sixty. My brother Marcus has a stent.
Clinician: I'd like an ECG today and a stress test. Before we do that, I need your MRN for the order. The system is down, can you read it off your wristband?
Patient: It says four four seven, two nine one, zero eight.
Clinician: Thanks. I'm also starting you on a baby aspirin. Dr. Brandt in cardiology will see you this week.
Patient: Can they text me? five one three, five five five, zero one seven seven.
Clinician: I'll put that on the referral. If the pain comes at rest, call 911.

transcript:
Clinician: Hi there. And this must be Amara. How old is she now?
Parent: Four, since July 22nd.
Clinician: Wonderful. Any concerns? Eating, sleeping, talking?
Parent: She's great. Picky with vegetables. Her older brother Jonah was the same.
Clinician: Totally normal. She's due for her booster shots today. The lot number on this vaccine box is four four one nine two, I'll record it.
Parent: Okay. Can I get a copy of her shot record for the school?
Clinician: Of course. What's the best email?
Parent: nkem.eze@outlook.com. And my name for the form is Nkem Eze.
Clinician: Perfect. Her growth looks right on track.

Clinician: Morning. What's going on with your back?
Patient: I lifted a box of tile at the warehouse on Monday, October 5th. Since then it's like a knife on the left side.
Clinician: Any numbness down the leg, any trouble with your bladder?
Patient: No, nothing like that.
Clinician: Good. That's reassuring. This sounds like a muscle strain. I'll give you a short course of an anti-inflammatory and a note for light duty.
Patient: My supervisor needs it faxed. And my name is spelled Siobhan Kearney, S I O B H A N.
Clinician: Got it. Home address for the work note?
Patient: 77 Brookfield Lane, Fairborn, Ohio 45324.
Clinician: Thank you. Gentle walking every day, heat, and no lifting over twenty pounds for two weeks.

transcript:
Clinician: How have the last six weeks been on the sertraline?
Patient: Better. I'm sleeping. I went back to choir.
Clinician: That's a big step. Any side effects?
Patient: A bit of nausea the first week, gone now.
Clinician: Any thoughts of hurting yourself?
Patient: No. Not since the spring.
Clinician: I'm glad. Let's keep the dose. Who's your support at home?
Patient: My partner, Jordan Pike. And my therapist at the county clinic.
Clinician: Good. I'll see you back on November 19th. If anything changes, the after-hours line is on your card.
Patient: Okay. For the record, I'm Avery Castellano, in case the portal still has my old name.

Clinician: Hi, I'm Keisha. You're here for burning when you urinate?
Patient: Yes, since Saturday. And I'm going a lot.
Clinician: Any fever, back pain, nausea?
Patient: No.
Clinician: Your urine dip shows signs of infection. I'll send a culture and start you on nitrofurantoin for five days. Any allergies?
Patient: Sulfa. It gave me hives.
Clinician: Noted. Can I confirm your details for the lab? Date of birth?
Patient: 2/14/1990.
Clinician: And the MRN on your card?
Patient: HL5520367.
Clinician: Great. If the culture changes anything, we'll call. Number?
Patient: 937.555.0164. It's Priya Raman, by the way, the receptionist had me as Priya Ramen.

Clinician: Mr. Bautista, your blood pressure today is 152 over 94.
Patient: It's always high here. At home it's lower.
Clinician: Have you been logging it?
Patient: My granddaughter Luz set up an app. She emails it to you.
Clinician: She does, I see the readings from September 15 through September 30. They're mostly in the 140s. That's still above where we want you.
Patient: So more pills?
Clinician: Let's increase the amlodipine to ten milligrams. And cut back on the salt. We'll recheck in four weeks.
Patient: Okay. Is my insurance still the same? Member ID MDX 830 447 105.
Clinician: It is. And you're still at 1902 Salem Avenue?
Patient: Yes. With Luz and my son.

Clinician: You tested positive on August 3rd, is that right?
Patient: Yes. I took the Paxlovid. The infection went fine, but I'm still exhausted.
Clinician: How are you sleeping?
Patient: Ten hours and I wake up tired. I'm a teacher, and I couldn't finish the first week of school.
Clinician: I want to check your blood count, thyroid and iron. We'll take it slow, a graded return to activity.
Patient: Can you write something for my principal?
Clinician: Yes. Full name for the letter?
Patient: Grace Whitfield-Osei.
Clinician: And your social, for the disability paperwork?
Patient: 523-71-4486.
Clinician: Thanks. I'll send the letter today.

Clinician: Let's look at that rash.
Patient: It showed up after we were camping at my in-laws' place near Yellow Springs.
Clinician: It's in a line on your forearm, with blisters. That looks like poison ivy.
Patient: That's what my husband Theo said.
Clinician: He's right. I'll prescribe prednisone, a short taper, and a cream. Wash any clothes you wore that day.
Patient: Will it spread?
Clinician: Not from person to person. It can look like it's spreading as the oil spots show up. Call us if it reaches your face. What number should we use?
Patient: nine three seven, five five five, zero one three one. Ask for Olivia.
